Getting Here

By air, car, and bus.

By Plane

Asheville Regional Airport (AVL) is the closest airport, about 15 minutes from the venue. It's served by American, Delta, United, and Allegiant with direct flights from Atlanta, Charlotte, Chicago, New York, and other hubs.

Charlotte Douglas (CLT) is a 2-hour drive and often has more flight options, especially if you're connecting. We recommend arriving Thursday evening if you can — Asheville is worth a night.

By Car

Riverbend Learning Center is in East Asheville, just off I-40. From I-40 East, take exit 55B (Swannanoa River Road) and head east. The center is on the left after about 1.2 miles, before the Swannanoa River bridge.

  • From Atlanta: ~3 hours via I-85 N and I-26
  • From Charlotte: ~2 hours via I-85 W and I-26
  • From Knoxville: ~1.5 hours via I-40 E
  • From Raleigh: ~4 hours via I-40 W

By Bus / Transit

Asheville's CAT (City Area Transit) Bus Route 9 runs along Swannanoa River Road and stops approximately 0.3 miles from the venue entrance. The walk from the stop is flat, paved, and takes about 5–6 minutes.

Greyhound serves Asheville from major southeastern cities. The Asheville bus station is about 4 miles from the venue; a rideshare from the station runs $8–12.

Rideshare & Taxi

Uber and Lyft are readily available in Asheville. From the downtown area (where most hotels are), rideshares to Riverbend cost roughly $10–15. From AVL airport, expect $18–25.

We're planning a conference carpool board — check the attendee communications in September for details.

Where to Stay

Lodging near the venue.

October is peak fall foliage season in Asheville — book early. The following properties are all within 20 minutes of Riverbend. Prices are approximate for October 2026.

Smoky Mountain Lodge

5 min from venue · From $89/night

The closest option. Basic, clean, and practical. No frills — perfect if you're arriving late and leaving early. Walking distance to a few good breakfast spots.

Aloft Asheville Downtown

15 min from venue · $150–$200/night

A solid mid-range option in the heart of downtown. Good if you want to explore Asheville's restaurants and bars in the evenings. Parking garage on-site ($18/night).

Grand Bohemian Hotel

20 min from venue · From $200/night

Upscale lodge aesthetic, mountain views, outstanding bar, and one of the best restaurant menus in town. Great for people who want to treat the trip as something more than professional development.

Black Mountain Campgrounds

10 min from venue · $25–$40/site

For attendees who want to camp — there are several well-maintained campgrounds along the Swannanoa Valley and in the Black Mountain area, about 10 minutes east. October camping here is cold at night (lows in the 40s°F) but genuinely beautiful. Bring a real sleeping bag.

Group block coming. We are negotiating a room block at the Aloft and will share a discount code in August. If you need accessible lodging, please contact us at hello@fieldnoteslive.org and we'll help coordinate.

Accessibility

The site is partially ADA accessible.

We want to be direct about what is and isn't accessible at the venue so you can plan accordingly.

Indoor Spaces

  • Main Hall is fully wheelchair accessible with automatic doors
  • Conference Rooms A and B are accessible via ramp
  • Pavilion is accessible (paved path from parking)
  • All accessible restrooms are near the Main Hall entrance
  • Hearing loop available in Main Hall for Day Two talks — bring compatible hearing aids or T-coil device

Outdoor Spaces

  • Outdoor Amphitheater: paved seating area is accessible; grass areas are not
  • River Loop Trail (Field Sessions): packed gravel, mostly flat, wheelchair accessible for about 0.8 miles. Steeper sections beyond that point are not accessible.
  • Pine Ridge Area (B2 session): narrow unpaved path, not wheelchair accessible. An alternative indoor track will be offered.
  • Outdoor Classroom: grass surface, partially accessible

Parking & Drop-Off

Six designated accessible parking spaces are located directly in front of the Main Hall entrance. Drop-off zone is marked and covered. Please indicate accessible parking needs during registration so we can reserve space.

Contact Us About Your Needs

We are committed to accommodating needs not listed here. If you have questions about specific accessibility considerations — captioning, dietary requirements, nursing space, quiet room access, or anything else — email us at access@fieldnoteslive.org by September 15 so we have time to prepare.

What to Pack

Field session gear suggestions.

Day One puts you outside for most of the morning and early afternoon. October in Asheville means pleasant highs in the low-to-mid 60s°F, with mornings in the mid-40s. Come dressed to be outside and comfortable for 3–4 hours. Field sessions run rain or shine.

Layered clothing (morning temps in the 40s–50s°F)
Waterproof jacket or rain layer
Sturdy shoes or hiking boots (no flip-flops)
Water bottle (at least 24 oz — there's a fill station on-site)
Sun protection (SPF 30+, hat, sunglasses)
Bug spray (October ticks are still active in WNC)
Notebook + pen (digital notes are fine, but paper is faster outside)
Small daypack or bag for your gear

Weather & Field Session Policy

Field sessions on Day One run rain or shine. This is not a drill — we will be outside in light rain, and we think it's worth it. Dress for the conditions; embrace the point. The only exception is a severe weather warning issued by the National Weather Service (lightning, high wind event), in which case we move to indoor alternatives. We'll communicate any changes via email and the on-site schedule board by 7:30 am on Day One.
